Hi Priya / Carlos —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our end and a proposed set of next steps so we can scope commercial options: 

Call recap (very brief):
- Primary use: user-facing summarization + search augmentation for Acme's Help Center (high interactivity, short prompts).
- Preferred SLOs: p50 ~ 45–60ms, p95 ~ 120ms (you flagged latency sensitivity).
- Integration plan: start with hosted Redwood API, then move to Dedicated GPU pool on Q3 if traffic ramps.

Pricing & volume questions we need to finalize:
1) Expected token volumes (we heard 100–400M tokens/mo as an initial band). Could you confirm a conservative and an aggressive monthly number?
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned a target of ~$0.8–$1.2 per 1M tokens as an anchor — want to confirm the exact target $/1M you need to see to get internal approval.
3) Budget cadence & procurement window: do you have a procurement/PO timeline (this quarter vs next)?

Attached is a quick econ worksheet where I sketched two paths: Starter path (no commit + credits for early months) vs Commit path (12‑month reserved with tiered unit pricing).

Requested next steps:
- Priya: confirm conservative/aggressive token bands and target $/1M.
- We (Ben + Marissa): draft a two-option commercial term sheet (starter credit vs 12‑month commit) and return by EOD Thursday.
- Schedule a 30m call with your procurement team if the commit path looks viable.

Attachments: acme_token_breakdown.xlsx (token bands + modeled P&L), redwood-startup-terms.pdf (startup program summary)

Best,
Jordan Blake

- Expected ramp (month 4–9): 280–320M tokens/mo

Target unit economics: our CFO has given us a target of $0.95 per 1M tokens as an internal threshold to move forward. If we can demonstrate a path to ~ $0.75–$0.85 with a 12‑month commit + modest volume growth incentives, that would be attractive.

Budget and procurement timing: procurement is aiming for a signed agreement by end of Q1 (March). We are able to accelerate if pricing and security/controls checks are straightforward.

Jordan —

Fwding my quick pricing thoughts so you can fold into the term sheet.

On Wed, Jan 13, 2027 at 09:27 AM Priya Shah <priya@acmeai.com> wrote:
> Token volumes (monthly):
> - Conservative (month 1–3): 120M tokens/mo
> - Expected ramp (month 4–9): 280–320M tokens/mo
> - Aggressive (steady state): 650M tokens/mo
>
> Target unit economics: $0.95 per 1M tokens target; would prefer ~$0.75–$0.85 with 12mo commit.

Pricing proposal (internal shortlist):
- Option A — Starter (low friction): no long-term commit, 2 months of $10k credits, standard hosted rates thereafter. This is useful to close quickly and get data.
- Option B — Commit 12mo: reserve 3.6B tokens upfront (12x 300M/mo anchor) with tiered pricing: $0.70 / 1M for volume up to 2B, $0.60 / 1M for next 1B, $0.50 /1M beyond that; include a 10% onboarding/implementation rebate and an SLA addendum. Effective blended target could be ~ $0.72–$0.78 depending on ramp.
- Option C — Multi‑year (24mo) (if they want deeper discount): negotiate a larger commit with an uptake clause and annual true‑ups; target floor ~$0.50–$0.65 /1M on blended if they lock 24mo and add usage guarantees.

Eligibility: startup program requires Series A or earlier, company registration, and a short intake form + one investor confirmation. We can fast‑track approval if they provide incorporation docs and cap table snapshot.

Next internal asks for you before we send:
1) Confirm whether 3.6B reserve (12x 300M) looks palatable to them as an anchor.
2) If they want 24mo, we need to understand expected churn risk and their runway to lock multi‑year.

I can join next week's call with procurement if needed.

-Ben
Sr. Sales — Redwood Inference
